video_title: Tyrese Haliburton and Reggie Miller Take the Court Together | Full 30-Minute Conversation

quotes.speaker: Reggie Miller
quotes.summary_phrase: Reggie Miller on the longevity of his iconic choke gesture
quotes.excerpt: I didn't think it was going to have the longevity that it did all these years.

text_blocks.speaker: Tyrese Haliburton
text_blocks.text: Did you ever think the choke would live on for so long?

text_blocks.speaker: Reggie Miller
text_blocks.text: No, I didn't. Because when I did it to our good friend Spike Lee, I didn't think it was going to have the longevity that it did all these years. I didn't think the cameras were really rolling because it was a free throw that was going on, and he and I were having our banter back and forth. But I didn't think it was going to have the legs that it did all these years. And I thought it was dead until someone had to bring it back.

quotes.speaker: Tyrese Haliburton
quotes.summary_phrase: Tyrese Haliburton on the organic nature of his choke gesture
quotes.excerpt: It can't just happen. You can't just do it. That's not cool.

text_blocks.speaker: Reggie Miller
text_blocks.text: For the record, because people always ask, you and I never had any conversation about this. No, it was like, but I had no idea.

text_blocks.speaker: Tyrese Haliburton
text_blocks.text: Yeah, but it's also like from the minute I got here and all the Knicks games and all those games, it's always like, you have to do it, Reggie, this, that. But it has to happen organically. Right, and that's what I kept saying. I kept telling my boys like, it can't just happen. You can't just do it. That's not cool. Right, and then the moment just happened the right way, and you were there, so it played all into it even better.

quotes.speaker: Reggie Miller
quotes.summary_phrase: Reggie Miller on Tyrese Haliburton's historic playoff run
quotes.excerpt: Your run during those playoffs, that's arguably the greatest run any player to have.

text_blocks.speaker: Reggie Miller
text_blocks.text: I tell people, your run during those playoffs, that's arguably the greatest run any player to have. Some of the shots you made were like incredible. Time, score, place, what's on the line. And in the playoff basketball, people make them during the regular season, that's one thing. You're on to the next city.

text_blocks.speaker: Tyrese Haliburton
text_blocks.text: In Cleveland, you purposely missed the free throw?

quotes.speaker: Tyrese Haliburton
quotes.summary_phrase: Tyrese Haliburton on the missed free throw against the Cavaliers
quotes.excerpt: As soon as I make the first one, I look, I'm like, miss it. They're like, absolutely not.

text_blocks.speaker: Reggie Miller
text_blocks.text: In Cleveland, you purposely missed the free throw?

text_blocks.speaker: Tyrese Haliburton
text_blocks.text: No, but you know what's funny. So, did I make the first one? I made the first one, too. So you're down two, and then you miss the second one. Yeah, but I'm telling them, I'm like, as soon as I make the first one, I look, I'm like, miss it. They're like, absolutely not. Don't miss it. So then, so then when I missed it and grabbed it, but you didn't miss it on purpose. No, no, no, no, no. I just missed it. No, I just missed it.

quotes.speaker: Tyrese Haliburton
quotes.summary_phrase: Tyrese Haliburton on working on the step-back left
quotes.excerpt: We were working on step-backs left because I was like, they're shading me left.

text_blocks.speaker: Tyrese Haliburton
text_blocks.text: Going into Game 2, we always work out early in the morning before the team gets to the gym. And we were working on step-backs left because I was like, they're shading me left. I can really get down and get out to my left. So we worked on that that morning. And I don't know what came to me. We live, it's so funny we think about, we talk about all the time, like just for some reason that day I kept saying, I think step-back left is going to be there today. And it just organically felt right to get back to my left hand and just shoot it.

quotes.speaker: Reggie Miller
quotes.summary_phrase: Reggie Miller on his favorite shot of his career
quotes.excerpt: I always tell people, the next one. The next one is the best one.

text_blocks.speaker: Reggie Miller
text_blocks.text: I get asked all the time, what was your favorite shot? Was it the 8.9, or was it the MJ shot, was it the bank against New Jersey? I always tell people, the next one. The next one is the best one. Because you set up the one versus Giannis Antetokounmpo, again, playoff basketball, everything's on the line, incredible comeback.

quotes.speaker: Tyrese Haliburton
quotes.summary_phrase: Tyrese Haliburton on iso against Giannis Antetokounmpo
quotes.excerpt: In that moment, that's all I'm thinking. And again, that's a situation of the game.

text_blocks.speaker: Reggie Miller
text_blocks.text: Gary Trent was initially guarding you. Did you want Giannis?

text_blocks.speaker: Tyrese Haliburton
text_blocks.text: Yeah, yeah, yeah. He had five fouls. In that moment, that's all I'm thinking. And again, that's a situation of the game is just going the right way. Like momentum is everything in basketball, you know? So I'm like, if I get him out, string him along and then they're giving me the opportunity to iso, just get to what I want to get to.

quotes.speaker: Reggie Miller
quotes.summary_phrase: Reggie Miller on the addictive nature of winning
quotes.excerpt: Winning and being successful and being on those stages, it's a drug and you always want it.

text_blocks.speaker: Reggie Miller
text_blocks.text: When you taste success, even though what came from that was defeat, you want that all the time. It's a drug. I tell people, winning and being successful and being on those stages, it's a drug and you always want it. So we took small steps of losing in the first round my first, you know, two or three years to the Bad Boys and Isaiah, we lost to Larry in Boston. But those were like stepping stones and I loved that atmosphere of, because playoff basketball, as you know, the best thing in the world. It's totally different from regular season.

quotes.speaker: Reggie Miller
quotes.summary_phrase: Reggie Miller on the defensive confusion of the Bulls
quotes.excerpt: I still can't understand what they were doing defensively. That's what always bothers me.

text_blocks.speaker: Reggie Miller
text_blocks.text: My question about the MJ play, I still can't understand what they were doing defensively. That's what always bothers me. Was it a miscommunication? Why was he on your top side to where you could get him off and get open? Because in my mind, I'm thinking, if I'm guarding you and the ball's being taken out over there, you're going that way. I'm going to do everything I can to push you that way.

quotes.speaker: Tyrese Haliburton
quotes.summary_phrase: Tyrese Haliburton on the evolution of defensive switching
quotes.excerpt: There was no switching across the floor. So, Harper was guarding me down low.

text_blocks.speaker: Reggie Miller
text_blocks.text: In 80s and 90s basketball, early 2000s, you guarded your position. One's guarded ones, two guarded twos. There was no switching across the floor. So, Harper was guarding me down low. And I think he assumed that MJ was going to switch, which Harper had guarded me all series, all series. Why would he assume?

text_blocks.speaker: Tyrese Haliburton
text_blocks.text: Yeah, it's just seeing the evolution of the game with the switching.
